source_message: Accepted “Read Daniel's hand edit to Chicken”.
result:
Verified the section against the ledger pixels rather than taking it on trust, and corrected the two claims that didn't hold.

**What the 2026-09-16 batch actually measures.** Three sheets in five minutes — neighbour, chicken, crow — with the "what were you fixing?" line left empty on all three, so it had to be read off the pixels. 84 pixels removed across 23 frames. Nothing drawn, nothing recoloured, no colour introduced. 83 of the 84 are `#f8f4e6`, the lightest colour on all three sheets, and every one sits in the rows where the figure meets the ground: the chicken's lowest two of fifteen, the crow's lowest two, the neighbour's lowest six of twenty-four. No figure's lowest row rose — the contact just narrowed. Silhouette changed on all 23 frames, interior shading on none. That section now says so, and says the guide has no rule for where a sprite ends and the ground begins. No amendment proposed, per the standing rule that the unsigned guide waits for the look session.

**Two things in the draft were wrong and are fixed.** It called the tomato "the sixth edited sheet" — nine sheets carry edits. And it gave the figure heights in bare parentheses next to pixel counts, so a reader couldn't tell which number was which. Both rewritten. The 146-pixel total across five actor sheets does hold, as do every per-frame number.

**What you should know.** This has happened on eight sheets now because the cause was never removed. Ravi found it on 2026-09-03: the generator clears the cream backdrop by flood-filling from the corners, and the anti-aliased pixels hugging each sprite's edge fall just outside the tolerance, so they survive as an opaque pale rim. He wrote and tested the fix — a second non-propagating pass — against twelve samples and couldn't apply it, because the pipeline script lives in your skills folder outside this repository and a drain worktree can't write there. So it sat, and three more sheets arrived with the fringe on 2026-09-16, and you erased it by hand again. The five actor sheets are clean at the contact rows today; the next generated sheet won't be.

One thing that complicates the reading, and I put it in the section: the fence sheet carries the same complaint in your same words away from any ground contact. So the colour is being removed wherever it's opaque and shouldn't be — on a figure, that's always the ground.

recommend.question: Fix the pale fringe at the art generator now, or wait for the look session to settle the ground-contact rule first?
recommend.answer: Fix it at the generator now, and keep the ground-contact rule for the look session.
recommend.why: The fringe is anti-aliasing residue nobody drew on purpose — removing it settles no question of taste, and leaving it means hand-erasing every future sheet.
recommend.instead: Hold the generator change until the look session, on the grounds that the rule might turn out to want some pale pixels in that zone — at the cost of you erasing the next batch by hand too.
